suggestion.title: Add a 'stacking check': log every batch on the old Chorkor too, and only count net wood saved
suggestion.why: In a 2026 Edinburgh study of mangrove-area projects in Sierra Leone and Guinea, improved fish-smoking ovens cut mangrove wood from about 7,084 kg to 420 kg per household per year, yet cookstove savings fell short because households kept using three-stone fires alongside the new stoves (adjusted usage only 44.5%). If a woman smokes half her catch on the SafeSmoke kiln and the rest on her old Chorkor, your per-batch kg-wood-per-kg-fish looks great while total wood barely falls. Verifiers and Article 6 buyers will ask exactly this, so measuring it now makes your savings claim credible.
suggestion.action: In part 2 and the pilot plan, add a 'Stacking check' box: (1) for each enrolled woman, record ALL batches for the 17 weeks, on the SafeSmoke kiln (sensor and scale) and on any traditional kiln (simple weekly self-report on the wood-bundles board, spot-checked by a Carbon Mother with the connected scale once a fortnight); (2) report two numbers: kg wood per kg fish on the new kiln, and total wood per woman per week before and during the pilot; (3) state the rule that carbon income and the 60% share are calculated on net wood saved per woman, not per-batch efficiency alone; (4) add one quiz question and one picture card explaining why old-kiln batches still count. Cite the Edinburgh 2026 study for the stacking risk and the oven savings.
suggestion.source: University of Edinburgh Business School (B-CCaS), Max Meyer (10 June 2026)

evidence.title: Sierra Leone and Guinea: improved fish-smoking ovens cut mangrove wood use 94% and give over half of a blue carbon project's reductions
evidence.summary: An Edinburgh Business School MSc study, written by an author now working for the project developer West Africa Blue, traced real impacts of cookstoves, fish-smoking ovens and solar salt in mangrove areas of Sierra Leone and Guinea (field data May–June 2025). A traditional banda burned about 7,084 kg of mangrove wood per household per year against 420 kg for the improved oven, a stated 94% cut. Sierra Leone's ovens account for 8.4 MtCO2e over 30 years, over half of the total. Cookstoves underperformed because households kept using three-stone fires alongside them (adjusted usage 44.5% across 67 communities).
evidence.use: Cite in part 1 and the Keta mangrove section as regional proof that fish-smoking ovens, not household stoves, drive the biggest wood savings, and use the 44.5% stacking finding to justify measuring whether women keep firing the old Chorkor.
evidence.source: University of Edinburgh Business School (B-CCaS), Max Meyer, thought-leadership article (10 June 2026)

evidence.title: GIZ/Climate Focus: carbon project outreach is often gender-blind, so invite women directly
evidence.summary: A GIZ Article 6 Capacity Building study by Climate Focus finds no mandatory gender rules across the voluntary carbon market and notes that cookstove projects still lack gender indicators; only 44% of cookstove projects report SDG 5 (gender) contributions. It cites evidence that women know much less about local projects than men, partly because household heads are assumed to pass information on. It recommends inviting women directly, timing meetings around their work, transport and safety, and more training for women in carbon accounting. It also flags that changes in who controls money can trigger gender-based violence.
evidence.use: Use in the carbon literacy section to justify direct invitations, market-day timing and Carbon Mothers training, and in part 4 to add a safeguard against household conflict over mobile-money payouts.
evidence.source: GIZ Article 6 Capacity Building Programme / Climate Focus, Interlinkages between gender and carbon markets (October 2025)

evidence.title: Climate Focus: benefit-sharing guidance for household energy carbon projects
evidence.summary: Guidance funded by FMO for cookstove and household-energy carbon projects. Its minimum standard is that stove users get a guaranteed level of benefits (for example a subsidised stove or an interest-free loan) whatever the project earns. It notes that cash payments to users are rare and the exception, partly because of long lead times and high transaction costs, and asks projects to be open about how revenue is shared and to run a clear, accessible, culturally appropriate grievance mechanism. An Ethiopian case sells credits at a Fairtrade minimum price, with a premium funding local training.
evidence.use: Cite it in part 4 to show that SafeSmoke's 60% cash-to-mobile-money share goes beyond the sector norm, and to justify a guaranteed minimum benefit (floor) that does not depend on credit sales.
evidence.source: Climate Focus (Pradines, Conway, Kovács, Galt), Feb 2025

evidence.title: Benin: QualiSani indirect-heat kiln brings PAH exposure from smoked fish to safe levels
evidence.summary: A Benin–Belgium team measured 15 PAHs in 46 samples of grilled pork, smoked fish and smoked-dried fish, and modelled exposure for 300 pork and 186 fish consumers with 10,000-run Monte Carlo simulations. The abstract reports PAH levels reduced by about 99% for smoked fish with the QualiSani kiln compared with traditional smoking. Margins of exposure were well above the EFSA 'low concern' level of 10,000, except for about 2% of high-end consumers. Full text is embargoed until January 2027.
evidence.use: In part 1, cite QualiSani as a West African indirect-heat design with peer-reviewed PAH results, and use its consumer-risk method (margin of exposure) as the model for SafeSmoke's food-safety claim.
evidence.source: Iko Afé et al., Regulatory Toxicology and Pharmacology 172, 106233 (2026)

evidence.title: KNUST: fish smoked with older Keta mangrove wood breaks the EU PAH4 limit
evidence.summary: KNUST researchers smoked Atlantic chub mackerel with red mangrove wood aged 8, 11 and 14 years, bought at Salo market in Keta, and tested PAHs at the Ghana Standards Authority. PAH4 rose with wood age: 3.63, 6.06 and 12.5 µg/kg, so only the 14-year wood exceeded the EU limit of 12.0 µg/kg. Benzo[a]pyrene stayed below 1.00 µg/kg. Cadmium exceeded EU limits in all samples. The study is small (six fish per group, one traditional oven), and the paper has some unit and limit inconsistencies, so treat it as a signal, not proof. The authors recommend restricting older wood and adopting indirect, low-emission smoking.
evidence.use: In part 1 (flexible fuel) and part 2 (scale log), record wood type and rough age for each batch, and cite this study when you explain why SafeSmoke tests PAH4 against the EU 12.0 µg/kg limit.
evidence.source: Boadu et al., Scientific African 31, e03217 (2026)

evidence.title: UN Article 6.4 market now has a free, independent grievance route for affected people
evidence.summary: The Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (Article 6.4) runs two complaint routes. The grievance route lets people and organisations in a project's affected area report harmful social, economic or environmental effects at any time during the crediting period, with no fee. Each case goes to a panel of three experts drawn from a roster of 30 selected in 2025. A separate appeal route against Supervisory Body decisions costs USD 30,000, waivable for vulnerable groups, and must be filed within 28 days (14 for issuance). Filing is by form and email, which is hard for women who do not read or use email. Date is approximate: the guide carries no date, and its files were uploaded in March 2026.
evidence.use: Inclusion / 'independent grievance line': name the A6.4 grievance process as the top rung of your grievance ladder and show how your local line (voice notes, own language) feeds it, so complaints can reach the UN level.
evidence.source: UNFCCC, Appeals and Grievances: A Step-by-Step guide (Article 6.4 mechanism), 2026

evidence.title: Improved Ahotor oven costs GHS 10,000, yet fishmongers earn under GHS 100 a day; a reporter found almost no users
evidence.summary: A Clean Air Reporting Project investigation found the Ahotor oven, sold in Ghana for more than seven years, priced at about GHS 10,000, while the women interviewed said they earn under GHS 100 a day. In Tema, Teshie-Nungua, James Town, Cape Coast and Elmina the reporter found no one using it; only one user turned up, in Sekondi-Takoradi, a fishmonger who nearly lost her sight to smoke. Women also complained the oven does not smoke fish the way they want. The Ministry of Fisheries said it was considering ways to help processors buy modern stoves. This is journalism, not a measured study.
evidence.use: Kiln and financing section: cite the price-to-income gap (roughly 100 days of income) to justify pay-as-you-go or carbon pre-finance, and the 'does not smoke well' complaint to justify a taste and colour test in the pilot.
evidence.source: Prince Owusu Asiedu, MyJoyOnline / Adom TV (Clean Air Reporting Project), 23 Mar 2024

evidence.title: Gold Standard D-SMART: an official rulebook for digital stove and fuel monitoring
evidence.summary: Gold Standard's new tool (v1.0, May 2026) sets rules for digital MRV of cooking and thermal projects: data-logging scales for digital kitchen performance tests, continuous stove monitors (temperature, infrared or current) that count cooking events per day, and a digital activity database. It asks for 90/10 precision with at least 50 units per stratum, keeps 'orphan' fuel readings (fuel logged with no cooking event) as fuel use rather than deleting them, and allows no claims if average use falls below 0.14 cooking events a day. Its end-user types include household, institutional and commercial.
evidence.use: Part 2 (Sensors): map your temperature sensor and connected scale to D-SMART's three components so the measured kg wood per kg fish is described as 'designed to D-SMART rules', not a home-made metric.
evidence.source: Gold Standard, Methodology Tool GS4GG PAA MT400-07 (D-SMART) v1.0, 5 May 2026

evidence.title: Nordic fund pays clean-cooking firms only for evidence of sustained use; 68% of buyers were women
evidence.summary: Nefco's Modern Cooking Facility for Africa reports over EUR 34 million committed to 22 companies by end-2025, with results-based payments linked to evidence of sustained stove and fuel use over time, using regular customer payments as a proxy. Over 68% of services in 2025 were bought by women as primary customers; 178,000 people gained access across Kenya, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe since 2023.
evidence.use: Benefit sharing: cite to justify paying the 60% share per logged batch (sustained use), not per kiln handed out, and to show funders already reward women-led uptake.
evidence.source: Nefco, MCFA Annual Results Report 2025 (22 Apr 2026)

evidence.title: World Bank USD 200m outcome bond pays upfront for Ghana clean cooking, repaid from Swiss ITMO sales
evidence.summary: The World Bank's Clean Cooking Outcome Bond front-loads money to UpEnergy's Ghana projects, released against pre-agreed milestones; investors accept a lower fixed return plus a variable return tied to sales of Article 6 credits (ITMOs) to Switzerland's KliK Foundation. Standard Chartered (Sept 2026) says USD 30.5 million was raised for devices in Ghana, aiming at 415,000 devices and 1.8 million t CO2 avoided; the World Bank page says over 400,000 systems for 1.3 million people.
evidence.use: Benefit-sharing section: cite as proof that 'upfront plus results' finance already works in Ghana's Article 6 market, and model SafeSmoke's pre-finance on milestone release (kilns built, baseline measured, batches logged).
evidence.source: World Bank feature 'Cooking up Change' (5 Dec 2025); Standard Chartered (24 Sep 2026)

evidence.title: Ghana offers Africa its Article 6 playbook after transferring 34,705 cookstove ITMOs
evidence.summary: At the AMCEN meeting beside COP31 (Antalya), Environment Minister Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings said Ghana is the first African country to complete authorisation, issuance, transfer and reporting of ITMOs under Article 6, transferring 34,705 ITMOs to Switzerland from a rural cookstove project. She offered to lead an AMCEN-African Group of Negotiators peer-learning programme on registries, project approval and accounting; Ghana already hosted Rwanda, Uganda, Sierra Leone and Mozambique in 2025.
evidence.use: Cite in 'Ghana market' and in your 'one umbrella programme across Africa' idea: Ghana is positioning itself as the Article 6 teacher for the continent, so SafeSmoke can pitch its rules and literacy kit as a Ghana-made template to share through that peer-learning channel.

evidence.title: Liberia: 28-tonne solar cold room for a women fish processors' association
evidence.summary: UNDP Liberia and the government commissioned a 28-metric-ton solar-powered prefab cold storage room in Robertsport on 12 March 2026 for the Robertsport City Women Association, certified by UNDP engineers and the fisheries authority NaFAA. It is community-owned and meant to cut post-harvest losses from spoilage; the release gives no loss figures.
evidence.use: Cite under the spoilage problem as a West African precedent for a women-owned add-on; list solar cold storage as a phase-2 option the 10% community fund could co-finance for bumper seasons.

evidence.title: Academic critique: refugee carbon projects risk weak consent and little cash for refugees
evidence.summary: Beuret, Fitzmaurice and Harvie (accepted in Race & Class) examine UNHCR's REP Fund pilots (Bidibidi, Kyangwali, Kigeme; about 90,000 households to get eco-stoves and fuels). By their own estimate the credits would cover only about 14% of current funding for the roughly 388,000 people at the pilot sites. They argue refugees' labour and stove use are the main input while only a small share of money reaches them, that many participants do not fully understand the carbon rights they sign over, and that cookstove credits may be overstated.
evidence.use: Use in Displacement and Inclusion as the critique you answer head-on: show that SafeSmoke pays each woman directly by logged batch, uses measured (not assumed) wood savings, and obtains consent the woman can explain back.
evidence.source: Beuret, Fitzmaurice & Harvie, University of Essex repository (accepted manuscript, Race & Class)

evidence.title: UNHCR energy report: carbon pilots for refugee and host households, and a refugee-host revenue rule
evidence.summary: UNHCR's Annual Report 2025 on Sustainable Energy (released May 2026) says its Refugee Environmental Protection Fund began pilots in 2025 in Bidibidi and Kyangwali (Uganda) and Kigeme (Rwanda), aiming at clean cooking for about 90,000 refugee and host households and an estimated USD 95 million in carbon revenue. A planned solar mini-grid in Pakistan gives 35% of its power free to refugee-run shops, bills host shops below the grid tariff, and is run by a Power Committee of refugee, host and private-sector members.
evidence.use: Cite in the Displacement and Inclusion sections as UN precedent for a written refugee/newcomer-host split and a mixed committee; it backs your host and newcomer community fund and guaranteed seats.

evidence.title: Sierra Leone mangrove project gives 200+ communities 40% of gross carbon revenue
evidence.summary: Carbon Market Watch reports a benefit-sharing deal between Africa Conservation Initiative and more than 200 communities in Sittia Chiefdom: communities get 40% of gross revenue and co-run a joint company that manages the money. It argues shares of gross revenue beat profit-based shares, which push risk onto communities and invite creative accounting, and notes Article 6.2 sets no benefit-sharing rules.
evidence.use: Your 60% is of 'net' carbon income: define net in one line (which costs may be deducted, with a cap) or show the women's share as a % of gross too, citing this as the model reviewers now expect.

evidence.title: UN Article 6.4 mechanism adopts two clean-cooking methodologies
evidence.summary: The Supervisory Body adopted its first two clean-cooking methodologies (efficient wood and charcoal stoves, and a wider switch to cleaner cooking) plus a tool for reversal risk. Both are described as household methods.
evidence.use: Fish smoking is a business use, so ask Ghana's Carbon Market Office whether commercial kilns fit under Article 6.4 or need the VM0050 SME route.

evidence.title: CSIR-FRI is testing three fish-smoking ovens in six communities
evidence.summary: CSIR-FRI, with the University of Bergen and the Fisheries Commission, is comparing the Chorkor, a redesigned (2022) Ahotor and a cheap retrofitted Chorkor with a fat tray in Akosombo, Kpong, Ahwiam, Joma, Vodza and Saltpond-Ankaful. PAH results are not yet published.
evidence.use: Your kiln must beat the cheap retrofit on cost per kg of wood saved. CSIR-FRI (Dr Amy Atter) is a natural design and PAH-testing partner.

evidence.title: Ghana's carbon market: 91 projects, 11 authorised
evidence.summary: UNDP reports 91 projects in Ghana's pipeline, 11 authorised for international transfer covering 12.7 million tonnes CO₂e, and 11,733 ITMOs delivered to Switzerland in 2025. New carbon market regulations are under legal review.
evidence.use: Problem statement: update the market numbers and cite this source next to the Carbon Market Office report.

evidence.title: Carbon credits are Africa's biggest bet for clean cooking
evidence.summary: AP reports that new policies across Africa have helped secure about $900 million in clean-cooking finance, with carbon credits the main engine, as long as buyers trust the credits.
evidence.use: Opening of your pitch: the money exists, and trust (your measured data) is what unlocks it.

evidence.title: Verra's VM0050 draft v2 covers small and micro enterprises
evidence.summary: The draft version 2.0 (9 July 2026) applies to households, community kitchens, institutions and small and medium-sized enterprises, including micro enterprises. Biomass stoves need at least 25% thermal efficiency, must pass a durability protocol, carry a permanent unique ID, and the project must give incentives to retire the old stove.
evidence.use: This is the strongest route for fish smokers as micro enterprises. Add 'unique kiln ID', 'efficiency test' and 'retire or retrofit the old Chorkor' to the kiln and sensor parts.

evidence.title: Paying carbon income straight to women's mobile money
evidence.summary: A CGAP Focus Note (July 2026) describes Carboneers' biochar project in Ghana paying carbon revenue into women's own mobile money accounts, which creates time-stamped records of who was paid. It recommends treating payment records as part of MRV, while noting they show participation, not empowerment.
evidence.use: Part 4: cite this Ghana example for paying the 60% to her own wallet, and add a short survey on how women use the money.

evidence.title: First fully digital cookstove credits issued by Gold Standard
evidence.summary: ATEC's eCook Bangladesh project had 1,667 tonnes approved under Gold Standard's digital MRV pilot. IoT SIMs on each stove sent signed, encrypted usage data, and 75% of credits were issued early on an interim track, before full verification.
evidence.use: Part 2: design the SafeSmoke sensor kit so its data is signed and sent automatically. Early (interim) issuance could bring income to the women sooner.

evidence.title: Senegal: 700 women fish processors use biogas from fish waste
evidence.summary: In Guet Ndar, Saint-Louis, a women's group runs 6 biodigesters feeding 10 cooking platforms, plus composting, reporting about 252 t CO₂ and 12 t methane avoided a year and fertiliser sales.
evidence.use: An idea for a later phase: turn fish waste into fuel or fertiliser at the landing site.

evidence.title: Ghana's first Article 6 cookstove deal cut its fNRB from about 80% to 30%
evidence.summary: Reporting on the Swiss-financed rural cookstove project says Switzerland set the non-renewable biomass fraction at 30% after developers pushed for nearly 80%, cutting projected savings from 3.2 to 1.3 million tonnes. Partners declined to share stove numbers.
evidence.use: Use 30% fNRB in your own estimate of credit income per woman, and promise open data: it's an integrity advantage.

evidence.title: AMS-II.G ruled out of the high-quality (CCP) label
evidence.summary: The Integrity Council approved Gold Standard's metered method, TPDDTEC v4.0 and Verra VM0050 v1.0, but rejected AMS-II.G and Gold Standard's simplified cookstove method for weak measurement of fuel use and stove use. CCP-labelled fNRB values will typically be below 0.5, against a market average of 0.86.
evidence.use: Part 2 and 'The opportunity': point to a CCP-eligible method and use a conservative fNRB in any credit estimate.
